content:
marie: Heads-up: eu-west GPU pool has been at ~98% for the last 12m. Streaming p99 latency jumped to 3.2s, streaming queue length ~1100, while batch throughput is mostly unaffected. Anyone watching?
kevin: saw the dashboards. looks like a handful of long-running streaming sessions holding KV caches and preventing fast preemption.
sophie: are these from a single customer or noisy tenants? any big prompt spikes?
marie: scatter of client IDs — not one tenant. net egress in the AZ is also high, saw TCP retransmits on ~2 nodes.
raj: copying network logs now. could be cross-AZ ingress causing slow tail latency which keeps streaming slots occupied.
infra-bot: deploy-bot detected 7 streaming pods in eu-west with >95% GPU memory and 500-800MB/s NVLINK trafffic. Monitoring alert: eu-west-gpu-pool.saturation > 0.9 for 10m.
kevin: proposal: enforce soft-preempt on streaming sessions older than 45s, and apply a reserve of 8 streaming tokens per GPU to keep tail slots free. That should lower p99 without killing throughput.
sophie: +1 but we should avoid hard-killing live user streams. soft-preempt means pause op and spill KV to blobstore, then requeue with high-priority short window?
marie: yep. we can checkpoint KV and return a small 503 with Retry-After for affected sessions, or continue with lower token allotment. Need config change in admission-controller.
raj: also thinking we should throttle new streaming connections at the gateway if egress packet loss > 1%. add a token-bucket tied to network health signal.
kevin: draft admission config (for testing):
```
{"policy":"soft_preempt", "streaming_priority":200, "batch_priority":100, "stream_reserve_per_gpu":8, "soft_preempt_threshold_s":45, "network_backoff": {"enable":true, "loss_pct_threshold":1.0, "rate_reduction_pct":30}}
```
marie: looks good. can we run in a canary AZ first? deploy to eu-west-1a only, 10% ingress, and watch p99 and user impact.
sophie: I'll run the canary. small checklist: 1) update admission-controller configmap, 2) rollout to 10% of gateway pods, 3) enable debug logging for preempt events, 4) hook metric to 'streaming.preempt.count' and 'streaming.requeue.latency'.
on-critical-note: +:thumbsup:
raj: if canary goes well, we should couple soft-preempt with a short-lived in-memory KV compression (reduce mem by 30%) to avoid excessive NVLINK writes. that buys more room without impacting client RT.
on-critical-note: :thinking_face:
kevin: quick command I ran to inspect pods:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep eu-west | grep streaming | awk '{print $1, $3, $6}' | head -n 10
# output: streaming-abc123 Running 98%
# streaming-def456 Running 96%
```
marie: sophie — can you flip canary now? tag me once done. I'll prepare runbook blurb for support and a canned message.
sophie: canary deployed to eu-west-1a at 14:32UTC. logging enabled.
oncall-bot: Incident task created: INC-2026-4723, assignee: oncall, priority: P2. https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-4723
kevin: monitoring: after canary, streaming p99 dropped to 1.1s in 1a, queue depth down ~70% on canary nodes. good signal.
marie: perfect. roll to rest of eu-west after 30m if metrics stable. also schedule a follow-up: investigate why NVLINK bandwidth spikes align with streaming tails. could be model KV thrashing.
raj: I'll open a profiling ticket for model cache access patterns.
sophie: rolling to remaining eu-west at +30m. will post updates.
marie: thanks team — also add a note to pricing/cost-analysis: reserve tokens will slightly raise cost per-request due to headroom, need to model impact.
kevin: noted. I'll run cost projection for 24/7 reserve vs dynamic reserve.
marie: closing thread for now, will update after full rollout.
